title: Godot drops frames using OpenXR with Vulkan on Wayland when at least one non embedded subwindow is open at application launch
body:
### Tested versions

Tested and reproducible in Godot 4.7 Beta 1-5, Dev 1-5; Godot 4.6.2

### System information

Godot v4.7.beta5 - Garuda Linux #1 ZEN SMP PREEMPT_DYNAMIC Tue, 02 Jun 2026 18:26:42 +0000 on Wayland - Wayland display driver, Multi-window, 3 monitors - Vulkan (Forward+) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3090 (nvidia; 610.43.02) - 12th Gen Intel(R) Core(TM) i9-12900K (24 threads) - 62.53 GiB memory - PulseAudio (44100 Hz, Stereo/mono); Also tested on X11 display driver

### Issue description

When running any scene in Godot while using VR (I explicitely tested OpenXR on Linux using the Valve Runtime) and while having an additional native Window open, the scene lags, and the VR display drops frames. This is not as visible on the preview VR view of either Godot or even SteamVR. However in practice it makes the VR application unusable.

**This happens using any Vulkan renderer (forward or mobile). This does not happen with the OpenGL Compatibility renderer.**

Minimizing the additional window improves this slightly, however opening it again causes it to lag again. 

However, reinitializing the window (closing and opening it completely again) completely fixes the issue. 



I used SteamVR 2.16.6 and a Valve Index. (I could retest it with other headsets if necessary.)

### Steps to reproduce

1. Prepare a VR headset to be able to run Godot in XR.
2. Play the provided demo project.
3. Notice how the text appears to jitter and lag / frames drop. (Feel free to also use the debugger, or the SteamVR widget)
4. Play around with minimizing and maximizing the secondary window.
5. Press Enter to hide (close) / unhide the additional window.
6. After reopening the window, the lags are gone.

---

In the provided video I hide the window once at around 1:05.
